Chapter 5: Aligning Actions with Personal Values
Now that you’ve learned how to notice, name, and create space from your emotions, let’s take the next step—figuring out what really matters to you, and using those insights to guide your actions. Think of your values as compass points. They’re what give your life direction and meaning, even when things feel uncertain or tough.
Too often, we end up drifting through life on autopilot—reacting to whatever comes our way or just following what other people expect. Sound familiar? It’s easy to end up feeling disconnected or even empty, because we’re not really acting in line with what’s most important to us. Emotional agility invites you to flip that script. Instead of letting life just happen to you, you get to use your values as a guide—for living with intention.
Here’s something to remember: values aren’t just goals to tick off your list. They’re ongoing qualities of action—like honesty, kindness, creativity, or courage. They’re freely chosen by you—not handed down or forced by anyone else. And the best part? They give you a sense of purpose that sticks, even when circumstances keep changing.
So, how do you actually figure out your core values? Start by thinking back to moments when you felt truly satisfied or proud. What were you doing? What qualities showed up in those moments? When you reflect on what actions felt the most meaningful, you’ll probably start to see the underlying principles that matter to you most.
Once you’re clear on your values, you can use them as a touchstone when you’re making decisions. When you hit a crossroads or feel a strong emotion, try asking yourself, “What action would line up with my values right now?” That simple question can cut through confusion and give you the motivation to move forward.
Let’s look at a couple of real-world examples. Imagine a leader who values transparency. They might choose to have an honest, maybe even tough, conversation with a team member who’s struggling—even if it’s uncomfortable. Or think about a parent who values connection. Even when they’re tired or stressed, they might put aside their phone and spend quality time with their child, because that’s what matters most to them.
Living in alignment with your values doesn’t mean you have to ignore your feelings or pretend everything’s fine. It’s about acknowledging how you feel, and then choosing responses that reflect what’s truly important to you. This way, you build up your sense of integrity and self-respect—even when things don’t go perfectly, or others criticize your choices.
Here are a few practical ways you can start living in sync with your values:
First, clarify your core values. Reflect on which qualities or principles matter most to you, and jot them down as a reminder.
Next, use your values as a guide. When emotions are running high, pause for a moment and ask, “What would my values have me do right now?”
And finally, make small, intentional choices. Look for everyday moments to act in line with your values—even in the little decisions.
Over time, these practices help you feel more grounded and give your life more coherence and meaning. Challenges stop feeling like roadblocks, and start becoming opportunities to reaffirm what matters most.
And here’s the real benefit: living in alignment with your values boosts your motivation and resilience. When your actions connect to a deeper sense of purpose, it gets a whole lot easier to push through setbacks and adapt when things change.
That’s the heart of emotional agility—the ability to move through life with flexibility, courage, and authenticity.
